title: 1962 FIFA World Cup
prose:
The 1962 FIFA World Cup was staged in Chile from 30 May to 17 June, the first and only time the South American nation hosted the tournament. Sixteen teams contested it, drawn into four groups of four; the top two from each group advanced to a single-elimination knockout stage of quarter-finals, semi-finals, a third-place match and the final. It was the first World Cup to use goal average to separate teams level on points, a tiebreaker that helped settle the group standings. The tournament was a notably defensive one: the scoring average fell to 2.78 goals per match, continuing a downward trend, while total attendance reached 893,172 across the competition, an average of about 27,912 per match.

Brazil, the reigning champions from 1958, arrived as favourites but lost their reigning star early when Pelé suffered an injury in the group stage and took no further part. Amarildo stepped in as his replacement. Garrincha became the driving force of Brazil's run, sharing the tournament's top-scorer total of four goals. He is widely regarded as the outstanding player of the competition, carrying the side after Pelé's injury, though no official Golden Ball existed in 1962. The top-scorer mark of four goals was shared by six players: Garrincha and Vavá of Brazil, Leonel Sánchez of Chile, Flórián Albert of Hungary, Valentin Ivanov of the Soviet Union and Dražan Jerković of Yugoslavia.

The final was played on 17 June at the Estadio Nacional in Santiago before 68,679 spectators, with Brazil meeting Czechoslovakia. Masopust opened the scoring for Czechoslovakia, but Brazil replied through Amarildo, Zito and Vavá to win 3–1 and claim a second consecutive title. In doing so Brazil became the second nation to retain the World Cup, after Italy in 1934 and 1938. Czechoslovakia finished as runners-up. The hosts, Chile, took third place by beating Yugoslavia 1–0, with Yugoslavia placed fourth. Among the tournament's enduring storylines was the so-called 'Battle of Santiago', the brutally violent group-stage match between Chile and Italy, which the hosts won 2–0.
